A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XBT research. All 11 pages in each version, including seven tables, five figures, equations, references, and supplementary material, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments, ablations, computational measurements, and supplementary zero-shot classification results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original retrieval, ablation, computational, and zero-shot classification results in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The two-stage XBT procedure is unchanged: text-only projection pretraining with noise, cross-modal contrastive training, visual prompts, LoRA, and selective layer-normalization tuning.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data and CC3M ablation, nocaps/Large-Flickr/Large-COCO retrieval coverage, continual-learning scenario, and supplementary ImageNet, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-Sketch classification evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Full-tune, LoRA-only, and Base in Table 1; Base in Tables 2 and 5; and the same original-model and computational comparisons elsewhere.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the supplement retain the same splits, sample sizes, model configurations, preprocessing, training budgets, and recall/accuracy metrics. The continual-learning and classification evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The noise, data-scale, data-source, and image-only pretraining ablations in Table 4 are identical. Qualitative retrieval, t-SNE visualization, computational analysis, and classification scaling analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the qualitative figures retain the same results. For example, Table 1's B32-to-L14 XBT backward-compatible R@1 remains 48.02 for text-to-image retrieval and 75.02 for image-to-text retrieval.

T1.justification: The compatibility criteria in Equations 1–2, projection and loss formulations in Equations 3–6, and embedding-distribution assumptions are unchanged. No formal results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about introducing XBT, efficient text-based alignment, preserving original model knowledge, and enabling backfill-free cross-modal retrieval.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of distribution mirroring, efficiency, and ablation findings. The supplementary discussion still acknowledges classification performance falling short of the new model and discusses improvement with more training samples.

D1.justification: Hardware, batch sizes, optimizer settings, LoRA configuration, projection architecture, augmentation details, and checkpoint/access information are unchanged in Section 4.1 and the supplement.

R1.justification: The same 48 cited works and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to backward-compatible training, continual learning, and transfer learning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Google DeepMind and University of Central Florida affiliations and an acknowledgments paragraph explaining the research's collaboration and completion context. Figure 1 receives a wording correction; the scientific narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption changes the incorrect panel references 'left/right' to 'above/bottom,' matching the existing vertical arrangement. Minor spacing and placement shifts accompany text reflow; all figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Figure 1's misleading panel directions and clarifies attribution through affiliations and acknowledgments. These provide a small improvement in presentation accuracy and transparency; the methods, empirical support, and scientific interpretations remain unchanged.
